rules.title: Motion seeking report on feasibility of banning algorithm-based rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Proposes that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on how many ownership and management entities use algorithm-based software to set rents, and whether a ban on using such software to set rents in the City is feasible. No ban is enacted or drafted.
rules.key_value: Report request on feasibility of a ban on algorithm-based rent-setting software
rules.citation: Los Angeles City Council Motion (Councilmember Heather Hutt), Council File 24-1031
rules.quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.
rules.coverage_text: Ownership and management entities using algorithm-based software to establish rents in the City of Los Angeles
rules.extraction_note: The document is a council motion stamped SEP 03 2024 requesting a departmental report; it does not itself establish a ban, prohibited conduct, or penalties. It is treated as pending because the text does not show adoption or any resulting ordinance. The council file number 24-1031 comes from the source URL, not the document body. The San Francisco ban mentioned in the text is background about another jurisdiction and is not extracted.
